newsitem.title: USA: Severe floods hit northern California wine country.
newsitem.headline: Severe floods hit northern California wine country.

text.p: Relentless rain pushed several northern California rivers over their banks on Wednesday, flooding homes and businesses and turning fields and vineyards into muddy brown lakes.

Northern California, which escaped relatively lightly from a series of punishing Pacific storms that caused havoc in the U.S. Northwest over the last week, was hard hit by the latest storm over the New Year's holiday.

The storm caused mudslides and sinkholes in Washington state and kept rivers in Washington and Oregon above or near flood level. Hundreds of people were forced out of their homes by floodwaters in California, Oregon and Washington.

At least 11 deaths are blamed on the storms that are estimated to have caused up to $250 million in damage in the three states. Gov. Mike Lowry has declared a state of emergency in 19 Washington counties and Gov. John Kitzhaber declared Jackson County in southern Oregon a disaster area.
In Caliifornia, up to six inches (15 cms) of rain fell in the wine country north of San Francisco in 24 hours, turning usually placid rivers into raging torrents.

The Russian River was 11 feet (3.3 metres) above flood stage in Guerneville on Wednesday afternoon and was expected to rise a further four feet (1.2 metres) by late evening, officials said. Rain was forecast for the rest of the week.
Homes and businesses in Guerneville, often hit by floods in the past, were flooded and scores of roads cut off by water. Stranded vehicles were abandoned.

"Roads in the area are going under water faster than we can keep a list of them. Residents are urged to evacuate as soon as possible," said Janice Atkinson, a spokeswoman for the Sonoma County Office of Emergency Services.

Some residents of the Guerneville area, 50 miles (80 kms) north of San Francisco, hurriedly evacuated, throwing possessions into bags, while others braved it out. Some townspeople found boats the best way to get around. About a foot of water covered the floor of a local grocery store.

The administrator of Sonoma County, which includes Guerneville, declared a local state of emergency. The National Guard brought in trucks, boats and helicopters to help evacuate residents. About 125 people were staying at a shelter in Sebastopol, one of several opened in the area.
The nearby Napa River also flooded, damaging homes and businesses and turning at least one vineyard into a lake.

Flooding was reported in many other parts of northern and central California. An overflowing creek flooded downtown Martinez, 25 miles (40 kms) east of San Francisco, and a hillside in Berkeley, near San Francisco, gave way, bringing a garage with a car inside down with it.

The storm downed trees and power lines, cutting off electricity to thousands. Pacific Gas and Electric Co. spokesman Cory Warren said 37,000 customers were without power in northern and central California. More than 143,000 customers were cut off at some time since New Year's Eve but most had had service restored, he said.
In Washington state, more than 100,000 customers in nine counties around Seattle were without electricity, Betty Werblun, a spokeswoman for Puget Sound Power and Light Co., said.
In Snohomish County northeast of Seattle, a search team was looking for three hikers who failed to return as planned on Sunday from a snowshoeing trip in the mountains.

Twenty-six homes had to be evacuated when a huge sinkhole opened in a street in Shoreline, a suburb north of Seattle. A mudslide knocked at least one home off its foundation in the wealthy Seattle neighborhood of Magnolia.

Several containers of hazardous material fell off a Burlington Northern Santa Fe freight train after four cars derailed near the town of Snohomish, about 35 miles (55 km) north of Seattle, but there were no spills, officials said.

Gus Melonas, a spokesman for the railroad, said the derailment apparently was caused by heavy rains that undermined the track. The derailment halted all freight traffic between Seattle and Everett 30 miles (50 km) to the north, although other lines were operating normally.
